The British Army’s approach to battlefield electrification, which outlines research and development plans through 2035 and supports the 2021 Ministry of Defense’s Climate Change and Sustainability Strategic Approach, emphasizes the need for U.K. defense to be a fast follower of commercial-sector advancements. An example that defense experts cite as a model are hydrogen generators, which were used to power the 2024 Isle of Wight music festival and which are capable of scaling to meet expeditionary or semifixed military operations, such as a divisional headquarters or a patrol base (Goodall 2025). In the northern EUCOM theater, risks to operational readiness and logistical challenges would be more acutely felt in Arctic operations, where extreme weather challenges could impact advanced energy technologies like batteries (Pechko 2025). D.4 Mitigations of Particular Importance to EUCOM With these challenges in mind, DOW could work with European partners to ensure energy infrastructure modernization and hardening could improve resilience in times of crisis or war. The Russia-Ukraine war demonstrated the vulnerability of transmission lines to drone attacks (Kyiv Post 2024) and exposed Ukraine’s aging transmission infrastructure as a weakness (Dreves, Fall, and McCan 2023). Moreover, hydrogen fuel cell EVs offer notable advantages in the EUCOM theater: the smaller battery size can reduce the need for rare earth minerals by 8–16 times compared to conventional battery EVs (Goodall 2025). Appendix E. New Technologies on the Horizon A number of technologies currently under development might address some of the U.S. Department of War’s (DOW’s) specific needs, including reliable power that is resistant to disruptions, energy generation with reduced visibility and detectability, and/or portable and easily transported and installed power technologies, including for use in remote locations. These innovations are at varied stages of commercialization and availability and are primarily driven by cost considerations. Strategic DOW investments in these emerging technologies could help to accelerate the time to advancement and commercialization for broader applications. E.1 Advanced Batteries Advanced battery chemistries and designs can provide batteries with lighter weights and improved performance, including higher energy densities (greater energy storage per unit volume or weight), faster charging, longer life cycles (functional lifetimes), and improved safety compared to standard lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries.
